and it is called \defd{the maximal modular decomposition} of~$G$.

nodes.name: Enriched modular decomposition
nodes.statement:
Formally, the \defd{enriched modular decomposition} of~$G$
is the pair~$(T,F)$
where~$T$ is the maximal modular decomposition of~$G$ (with~$L(T)=V(G)$)
and~$F\subset V(T)\times V(T)$
is a binary relation,
that relates a pair~$(s,t)$ of nodes of~$T$,
denoted $st\in F$,
exactly when~$s$ and~$t$ are siblings and~$\fullsucc{L(T_s)}{L(T_t)}$.
nodes.statement_short: The maximal modular decomposition T with a relation F linking siblings s, t whose leaf sets are fully adjacent from s to t.

nodes.name: m-edges
nodes.statement: The elements of~$F$ are called \defd{$\mathsf{m}$-edges}.

nodes.name: Modules form a weakly-partitive family
nodes.statement:
It should be mentioned that the family of all non-empty modules of~$G$
is known to be weakly-partitive (or even partitive when~$G$ is undirected).
In particular, the maximal modular decomposition~$T$ of~$G$
is the laminar tree induced by the family of strong modules.
conclusions:
the family of all non-empty modules of~$G$
is known to be weakly-partitive (or even partitive when~$G$ is undirected)

the maximal modular decomposition~$T$ of~$G$
is the laminar tree induced by the family of strong modules

nodes.name: Enriched modular decompositions as {ancestor, m-edge}-structures
nodes.statement:
To model enriched modular decompositions as relational structures
we use the relational vocabulary $\{\mathsf{ancestor}, \ensuremath{\textsf{m}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$
where $\mathsf{ancestor}$ and $\ensuremath{\textsf{m}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace$ are two binary relation names.
An enriched modular decomposition $(T,F)$ of a graph $G$
is modeled by the {$\{\mathsf{ancestor}, \ensuremath{\textsf{m}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$}-structure $\mathbb{M}$
with universe $U_{\mathbb{M}}=V(T)$,
$\mathsf{ancestor}_{\mathbb{M}}$ being the set of pairs $(s,t)$
for which~$s$ is an ancestor of~$t$ in~$T$,
and $\ensuremath{\textsf{m}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace_{\mathbb{M}}$ being the set of all pairs $(s,t)$
such that $st\in F$
(in particular, $s$ and~$t$ are siblings in~$T$).

nodes.name: CMSO[2]-transduction of the enriched modular decomposition
nodes.statement:
There exists a non-deterministic \CMSO[2]-transduction $\tau$
    such that for every directed graph $G$ represented as the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$-structure $\mathbb{G}$,
    $\tau(\mathbb{G})$ is non-empty
    and every output in~$\tau(\mathbb{G})$ is equal to some $\{\mathsf{ancestor},\ensuremath{\textsf{m}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$-structure $\mathbb{M}$
    representing the enriched modular decomposition~$(T,F)$ of $G$.
nodes.statement_short: A non-deterministic CMSO[2]-transduction outputs the enriched modular decomposition of any directed graph.
assumptions: for every directed graph $G$ represented as the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$-structure $\mathbb{G}$
conclusions:
$\tau(\mathbb{G})$ is non-empty
    and every output in~$\tau(\mathbb{G})$ is equal to some $\{\mathsf{ancestor},\ensuremath{\textsf{m}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$-structure $\mathbb{M}$
    representing the enriched modular decomposition~$(T,F)$ of $G$.
nodes.label: thm:transduce modular decomposition

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.4
nodes.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph represented by the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$-structure $\mathbb{G}$.
    Several objects are associated to~$G$,
    and each of them can be described by a structure:
    \begin{itemize}[nosep]
        \item let~$\mathcal{M}$ be the family of non-empty modules of~$G$
            and let~$\mathbb{S}$ be the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{SET}}\xspace\}$-structure
            modeling the weakly-partitive set system $(V(G),\mathcal{M})$
            with~$U_{\mathbb{S}}=V(G)$;
        \item let~$T$ be the laminar tree induced by the weakly-partitive family~$\mathcal{M}$
            and let~$\mathbb{T}$ be the $\{\mathsf{ancestor}\}$-structure
            modeling it with~$U_{\mathbb{T}}=V(T)$ and~$L(T)=V(G)\subset U_{\mathbb{T}}$;
        \item let~$F$ be the $\mathsf{m}$-edge relation,
            namely the subset of~$V(T)\times V(T)$ such that~$(T,F)$
            is the maximal modular decomposition of~$G$,
            and let~$\mathbb{M}$ be the $\{\mathsf{ancestor},\ensuremath{\textsf{m}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$-structure
            modeling it with~$\mathbb{T}\sqsubset\mathbb{M}$ and $U_{\mathbb{T}}=U_{\mathbb{M}}$.
    \end{itemize}
    Our \CMSO[2]-transduction is obtained by composing the three following transductions:
    \begin{itemize}[nosep]
        \item$\tau_1$: an \ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace-interpretation which outputs the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{edge}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathsf{SET}}\xspace\}$-structure $\mathbb{G}\sqcup\mathbb{S}$ from~$\mathbb{G}$;
        \item$\tau_2$: the non-deterministic \CMSO[2]-transduction given by \autoref{lem:transduce laminar tree induced by weakly-partitive family}
            which produces the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{edge}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathsf{SET}}\xspace,\mathsf{ancestor}\}$-structure $\mathbb{G}\sqcup\mathbb{S}\sqcup\mathbb{T}$ from $\mathbb{G}\sqcup\mathbb{S}$;
        \item$\tau_3$: an \ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace-interpretation which outputs the $\{\mathsf{ancestor},\ensuremath{\textsf{m}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$-structure $\mathbb{M}$ from $\mathbb{G}\sqcup\mathbb{S}\sqcup\mathbb{T}$.
    \end{itemize}

    In order to define $\tau_1$ it is sufficient to observe that
    there exists an \ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace-formula $\phi_{\ensuremath{\mathsf{SET}}\xspace}(Z)$
    with one monadic free-variable,
    which is satisfied exactly when~$Z$ is a non-empty module of~$G$.
    Then, since~$\tau_2$ is given by \autoref{lem:transduce laminar tree induced by weakly-partitive family},
    it only remains to define~$\tau_3$.
    Given an inner node~$t$,
    we can select, within \ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace,
    the set~$L(T_t)$ of leaves of the subtree rooted in~$t$.
    We thus assume a function~$\ensuremath{\mathsf{leafset}}\xspace$,
    with one first-order free-variable
    which returns the set of leaves of the subtree rooted at the given node.
    Equipped with this function,
    we can define the \ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace-formula $\phi_{\ensuremath{\textsf{m}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace}$
    which selects pairs~$(s,r)$ of siblings
    such that~$sr\in F$.
    Remember that this happen exactly when there exist $u\in L(T_s)$ and~$v\in L(T_r)$
    such that~$uv\in E(G)$.
    Hence, $\phi_{\ensuremath{\textsf{m}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace}$ could be defined as:
    \begin{align*}
        \phi_{\ensuremath{\textsf{m}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace}(s, r):=
            s\neq r
            \:\land\:
            &
            \exists t\:
            \big(\ensuremath{\mathsf{parent}}\xspace(t,s)\land\ensuremath{\mathsf{parent}}\xspace(t,r)\big)\land
            \\*&
            \exists x\exists y\big(x\in\ensuremath{\mathsf{leafset}}\xspace(s)\land y\in\ensuremath{\mathsf{leafset}}\xspace(r)\land \ensuremath{\mathsf{edge}}\xspace(x,y)\big).
    \end{align*}
    Once defined, the \ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace-interpretation~$\tau_3$
    simply drops all non-necessary relations and predicates
    (namely~$\ensuremath{\mathsf{edge}}\xspace$ and~$\ensuremath{\mathsf{SET}}\xspace$)
    and keeps only the~$\mathsf{ancestor}$ and~$\ensuremath{\textsf{m}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace$ relations.
nodes.statement_short: Compose an MSO-interpretation defining modules, the Lemma 4.1 transduction of the strong-module laminar tree, and an MSO-interpretation defining m-edges.

nodes.name: Associated structures
nodes.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph represented by the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$-structure $\mathbb{G}$.
    Several objects are associated to~$G$,
    and each of them can be described by a structure:
    \begin{itemize}[nosep]
        \item let~$\mathcal{M}$ be the family of non-empty modules of~$G$
            and let~$\mathbb{S}$ be the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{SET}}\xspace\}$-structure
            modeling the weakly-partitive set system $(V(G),\mathcal{M})$
            with~$U_{\mathbb{S}}=V(G)$;
        \item let~$T$ be the laminar tree induced by the weakly-partitive family~$\mathcal{M}$
            and let~$\mathbb{T}$ be the $\{\mathsf{ancestor}\}$-structure
            modeling it with~$U_{\mathbb{T}}=V(T)$ and~$L(T)=V(G)\subset U_{\mathbb{T}}$;
        \item let~$F$ be the $\mathsf{m}$-edge relation,
            namely the subset of~$V(T)\times V(T)$ such that~$(T,F)$
            is the maximal modular decomposition of~$G$,
            and let~$\mathbb{M}$ be the $\{\mathsf{ancestor},\ensuremath{\textsf{m}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$-structure
            modeling it with~$\mathbb{T}\sqsubset\mathbb{M}$ and $U_{\mathbb{T}}=U_{\mathbb{M}}$.
    \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the module system, its laminar tree, and the m-edge structure.

nodes.name: Module set system
nodes.statement:
let~$\mathcal{M}$ be the family of non-empty modules of~$G$
            and let~$\mathbb{S}$ be the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{SET}}\xspace\}$-structure
            modeling the weakly-partitive set system $(V(G),\mathcal{M})$
            with~$U_{\mathbb{S}}=V(G)$;
nodes.statement_short: The set system of non-empty modules as a SET-structure.

nodes.name: Laminar tree
nodes.statement_short: The laminar tree induced by the modules.

nodes.name: m-edge structure
nodes.statement_short: The m-edge relation and its structure.

nodes.name: Three-stage composition
nodes.statement_short: The transduction composes tau_1, tau_2, tau_3.

nodes.name: tau_1
nodes.statement: $\tau_1$: an \ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace-interpretation which outputs the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{edge}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathsf{SET}}\xspace\}$-structure $\mathbb{G}\sqcup\mathbb{S}$ from~$\mathbb{G}$;
nodes.statement_short: MSO-interpretation adding the module set system.

nodes.name: tau_2
nodes.statement:
$\tau_2$: the non-deterministic \CMSO[2]-transduction given by \autoref{lem:transduce laminar tree induced by weakly-partitive family}
            which produces the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{edge}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathsf{SET}}\xspace,\mathsf{ancestor}\}$-structure $\mathbb{G}\sqcup\mathbb{S}\sqcup\mathbb{T}$ from $\mathbb{G}\sqcup\mathbb{S}$;
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 4.1 adds the laminar tree.

nodes.name: tau_3
nodes.statement:
$\tau_3$: an \ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace-interpretation which outputs the $\{\mathsf{ancestor},\ensuremath{\textsf{m}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$-structure $\mathbb{M}$ from $\mathbb{G}\sqcup\mathbb{S}\sqcup\mathbb{T}$.
    \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: MSO-interpretation outputting the m-edge structure.

nodes.name: Define tau_1
nodes.statement:
In order to define $\tau_1$ it is sufficient to observe that
    there exists an \ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace-formula $\phi_{\ensuremath{\mathsf{SET}}\xspace}(Z)$
    with one monadic free-variable,
    which is satisfied exactly when~$Z$ is a non-empty module of~$G$.
    Then, since~$\tau_2$ is given by \autoref{lem:transduce laminar tree induced by weakly-partitive family},
    it only remains to define~$\tau_3$.
nodes.statement_short: Modules are MSO-definable; tau_2 is given by Lemma 4.1.

nodes.name: leafset function
nodes.statement:
Given an inner node~$t$,
    we can select, within \ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace,
    the set~$L(T_t)$ of leaves of the subtree rooted in~$t$.
    We thus assume a function~$\ensuremath{\mathsf{leafset}}\xspace$,
    with one first-order free-variable
    which returns the set of leaves of the subtree rooted at the given node.
nodes.statement_short: Leaf sets of subtrees are MSO-selectable.

nodes.name: Define m-edge formula
nodes.statement:
Equipped with this function,
    we can define the \ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace-formula $\phi_{\ensuremath{\textsf{m}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace}$
    which selects pairs~$(s,r)$ of siblings
    such that~$sr\in F$.
    Remember that this happen exactly when there exist $u\in L(T_s)$ and~$v\in L(T_r)$
    such that~$uv\in E(G)$.
    Hence, $\phi_{\ensuremath{\textsf{m}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace}$ could be defined as:
    \begin{align*}
        \phi_{\ensuremath{\textsf{m}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace}(s, r):=
            s\neq r
            \:\land\:
            &
            \exists t\:
            \big(\ensuremath{\mathsf{parent}}\xspace(t,s)\land\ensuremath{\mathsf{parent}}\xspace(t,r)\big)\land
            \\*&
            \exists x\exists y\big(x\in\ensuremath{\mathsf{leafset}}\xspace(s)\land y\in\ensuremath{\mathsf{leafset}}\xspace(r)\land \ensuremath{\mathsf{edge}}\xspace(x,y)\big).
    \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Siblings form an m-edge iff some edge goes between their leaf sets.

nodes.name: Drop auxiliary relations
nodes.statement:
Once defined, the \ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace-interpretation~$\tau_3$
    simply drops all non-necessary relations and predicates
    (namely~$\ensuremath{\mathsf{edge}}\xspace$ and~$\ensuremath{\mathsf{SET}}\xspace$)
    and keeps only the~$\mathsf{ancestor}$ and~$\ensuremath{\textsf{m}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace$ relations.
nodes.statement_short: tau_3 keeps only ancestor and m-edge.

nodes.name: Recovering a graph from its enriched modular decomposition
nodes.statement:
Notice that it is routine to design a deterministic \ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace-transduction which,
given an $\{\mathsf{ancestor},\ensuremath{\textsf{m}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$-structure $\mathbb{M}$
representing an enriched modular decomposition of some directed graph~$G$,
produces the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$-structure $\mathbb{G}$ representing~$G$.
conclusions: it is routine to design a deterministic \ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace-transduction

nodes.name: Sibling graphs at degenerate and linear nodes
nodes.statement:
Let~$G$ be a graph, $(T,F)$ be its modular decomposition,
and~$(T,\lambda,<)$ be the weakly-partitive tree induced by the (weakly-partitive) family of its modules.
Let~$t$ be an inner node of~$T$, let~$\mathcal{C}$ be its set of children,
and let~$C$ be the graph~$\big(V(T)\setminus L(T), F\big)\left[\mathcal{C}\right]$ induced by~$F$ on the set of children of~$t$.
It can be checked that,
if~$\lambda(t)=\ensuremath{\mathsf{degenerate}}\xspace$ then~$C$ is either a clique or an independant,
and if~$\lambda(t)=\ensuremath{\mathsf{linear}}\xspace$ then~$C$ is a \emph{tournament consistent with~$<_t$}
({\em i.e.}, for every $x,y\in\mathcal{C}$, $xy$ is an edge of~$C$ if and only if\xspace $x<_t y$)
or with the inverse of~$<_t$.
assumptions:
Let~$G$ be a graph, $(T,F)$ be its modular decomposition,
and~$(T,\lambda,<)$ be the weakly-partitive tree induced by the (weakly-partitive) family of its modules.
$\lambda(t)=\ensuremath{\mathsf{degenerate}}\xspace$
$\lambda(t)=\ensuremath{\mathsf{linear}}\xspace$
conclusions: $C$ is either a clique or an independant
$C$ is a \emph{tournament consistent with~$<_t$}

assumptions: $\lambda(t)=\ensuremath{\mathsf{degenerate}}\xspace$
conclusions: $C$ is either a clique or an independant

assumptions: $\lambda(t)=\ensuremath{\mathsf{linear}}\xspace$
conclusions: $C$ is a \emph{tournament consistent with~$<_t$}

nodes.name: Refined weakly-partitive tree
nodes.statement:
In the former case,
we can refine the $\ensuremath{\mathsf{degenerate}}\xspace$ label into~$\ensuremath{\mathsf{series}}\xspace$ and~$\ensuremath{\mathsf{parallel}}\xspace$ labels,
thus expressing that~$C$ is a clique or an independent, respectively.
In the latter case, up-to reversing~$<_t$,
we can ensure that~$C$ is a tournament consistent with~$<_t$.
This yields a refined weakly-partitive tree~$(T,\gamma,<)$,
where~$\gamma$ maps inner nodes to $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{series}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathsf{parallel}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathsf{prime}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathsf{linear}}\xspace\}$
and~$<$ is the order $\bigcup_{t\in\gamma^{-1}(\ensuremath{\mathsf{linear}}\xspace)}<_t$
which ensures that tournaments are consistent with the corresponding $<_t$.
nodes.statement_short: Refine degenerate labels into series/parallel and orient linear orders to match tournaments, giving (T, gamma, <).

nodes.name: Directed cograph and cotree
nodes.statement:
In particular, if no nodes of~$T$ is labeled by~$\ensuremath{\mathsf{prime}}\xspace$,
$(T,F)$ and thus~$G$ is fully characterized by~$(T,\gamma,<)$.
Graphs for which this property holds
are known as \defd{directed cographs},
and can be described by the refined weakly-partitive tree, called \defd{cotree}, explained above and formalized in the following statement.
nodes.statement_short: Directed cographs are graphs whose modular decomposition has no prime node; their refined tree is the cotree.

nodes.name: Cotree characterisation of directed cographs
nodes.statement:
Let~$G$ be a directed cograph and let~$T$ be the laminar tree induced by the family of its strong modules.
    There exists a unique total labeling~$\lambda$ from the set~$V(T)\setminus L(T)$ of inner nodes of~$T$
    to the set $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{series}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathsf{parallel}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathsf{linear}}\xspace\}$ of labels,
    and, for each inner node $t\in\lambda^{-1}(\ensuremath{\mathsf{linear}}\xspace)$,
    a unique linear ordering~$<_t$ of its children,
    such that every inner node having exactly two children is labeled $\ensuremath{\mathsf{series}}\xspace$ or $\ensuremath{\mathsf{parallel}}\xspace$,
    and the following condition is satisfied:
    \begin{itemize}[nosep]
        \item for every two leaves~$x$ and~$y$ of~$T$,
            denoting by~$t$ their least common ancestor,
            $xy$ is an edge of~$G$
            if and only if\xspace
            either~$t$ is labeled by~$\ensuremath{\mathsf{linear}}\xspace$ and~$x<_ty$,
            or~$t$ is labeled by~$\ensuremath{\mathsf{series}}\xspace$.
    \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: A directed cograph is described by its strong-module tree with unique series/parallel/linear labels and orders determining adjacency at least common ancestors.
assumptions: Let~$G$ be a directed cograph and let~$T$ be the laminar tree induced by the family of its strong modules.
conclusions: There exists a unique total labeling~$\lambda$
nodes.label: thm:cotree

nodes.name: Cotrees as {ancestor, series, eps-ord}-structures
nodes.statement:
We naturally model cotrees as $\{\mathsf{ancestor},\ensuremath{\mathsf{series}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\varepsilon\text-\mathsf{ord}}\xspace\}$-structures as follow.
A cotree $(T,\gamma,<)$ is modeled by~$\mathbb{C}$
where~$U_{\mathbb{C}}=V(T)$, $\ensuremath{\mathsf{series}}\xspace_{\mathbb{C}}=\gamma^{-1}(\ensuremath{\mathsf{series}}\xspace)$, and $\ensuremath{\varepsilon\text-\mathsf{ord}}\xspace_{\mathbb{C}}=\{(x,y)\mid x<y\}$.

nodes.name: Derivation of Corollary 4.6
nodes.statement:
Based on \autoref{thm:cotree} and as a consequence of \autoref{thm:transduce modular decomposition},
we can design a \CMSO[2]-transduction which produces the cotree of a cograph~$G$ from~$G$.
nodes.statement_short: Combine Theorem 4.4 with the cotree characterisation of Theorem 4.5.

nodes.name: CMSO[2]-transduction of cotrees
nodes.statement:
There exists a non-deterministic \CMSO[2]-transduction~$\tau$
    such that, for each cograph~$G$ modeled by the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$-structure~$\mathbb{G}$,
    $\tau(\mathbb{G})$ is non-empty
    and every output in~$\tau(\mathbb{G})$ is equal to some $\{\mathsf{ancestor},\ensuremath{\mathsf{series}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\varepsilon\text-\mathsf{ord}}\xspace\}$-structure~$\mathbb{C}$
    representing the cotree~$(T,\gamma,<)$ of~$G$.
assumptions: for each cograph~$G$ modeled by the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$-structure~$\mathbb{G}$
conclusions:
$\tau(\mathbb{G})$ is non-empty
    and every output in~$\tau(\mathbb{G})$ is equal to some $\{\mathsf{ancestor},\ensuremath{\mathsf{series}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\varepsilon\text-\mathsf{ord}}\xspace\}$-structure~$\mathbb{C}$
    representing the cotree~$(T,\gamma,<)$ of~$G$.
nodes.label: thm:transduce cotree

nodes.name: Bipartition system
nodes.statement:
A \emph{bipartition system} is a pair $(U,\mathcal{B})$ consisting of a finite set $U$, the \emph{universe}, and a family $\mathcal{B}$ of bipartitions of $U$ such that $\{\emptyset,U\}\notin\mathcal{B}$ and
$\{\{a\},U\setminus \{a\}\}\in \mathcal{B}$ for all $a\in U$.

nodes.name: Bipartition systems as {BIPART}-structures
nodes.statement:
To model bipartition systems, we use the extended vocabulary~$\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{BIPART}}\xspace\}$
where $\ensuremath{\mathsf{BIPART}}\xspace$ is a set predicate name of arity~$2$.
A bipartition system~$(U,\mathcal{B})$ is thus naturally modeled
as the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{BIPART}}\xspace\}$-structure $\mathbb{B}$
with universe~$U_{\mathbb{B}}=U$
and interpretation~$\ensuremath{\mathsf{BIPART}}\xspace_{\mathbb{B}}=\mathcal{B}$.

nodes.name: Overlapping bipartitions
nodes.statement: Two bipartitions $\{X,Y\}$ and $\{X',Y'\}$ of a set $U$ \emph{overlap} if the four sets $X\cap X'$, $X\cap Y'$, $Y\cap X'$ and $Y\cap Y'$ are non-empty.

nodes.name: Laminar bipartition family
nodes.statement:
A bipartition family is said to be \emph{laminar} (aka \emph{overlap-free})
if no two bipartitions in $\mathcal{B}$ overlap.
By extension, we call a family $\mathcal{B}$ of bipartition of a set $U$ \emph{laminar}
whenever $(U,\mathcal{B})$ is a bipartition system which is laminar.

nodes.name: Laminar tree of a bipartition system
nodes.statement: The tree $T$, called the \emph{laminar tree induced by $(U,\mathcal{B})$} (or \emph{laminar tree of $(U,\mathcal{B})$}), associated with a laminar bipartition system $(U,\mathcal{B})$ is unrooted, each element of $U$ corresponds to a leaf of $T$ and for each bipartition $\{X,Y\}$ in $\mathcal{B}$ there is exactly one edge $e$ such that $X=L(T_1)$ and $Y=L(T_2)$ for the two connected components $T_1,T_2$ of $T-e$.
nodes.statement_short: The unrooted tree with the universe as leaves whose edge cuts are exactly the bipartitions of the laminar system.

nodes.name: Weakly-bipartitive bipartition system
nodes.statement: A bipartition system $(U,\mathcal{B})$ is said to be \emph{weakly-bipartitive} if for every two overlapping bipartitions $\{X,Y\},\{X',Y'\}\in \mathcal{B}$, the biparitions $\{X\cup X',Y\cap Y'\}$, $\{X\cup Y',Y\cap X'\}$, $\{Y\cup X', X\cap Y'\}$ and $\{Y\cup Y', X\cap X'\}$ are in $\mathcal{B}$.

nodes.name: Bipartitive bipartition system
nodes.statement:
It is \emph{bipartitive}, if additionally for every two overlapping bipartitions $\{X,Y\},\{X',Y'\}\in \mathcal{B}$,
the bipartition $\{X\bigtriangleup X', Y\bigtriangleup Y'\}$ is also in $\mathcal{B}$.
By extension, we call a family $\mathcal{B}$ of bipartitions of a set $U$ \emph{weakly-bipartitive} or \emph{bipartitive} whenever $(U,\mathcal{B})$ is a bipartition system which is weakly-bipartitive or partitive, respectively.

nodes.name: Strong bipartition
nodes.statement: A bipartition $\{X,Y\}$ of a bipartition system~$(U,\mathcal{B})$ is said to be \emph{strong} if $\{X,Y\}$ does not overlap with any other bipartition in $\mathcal{B}$.

nodes.name: Family of strong bipartitions
nodes.statement: We denote the subfamily of strong bipartitions in $\mathcal{B}$ by $\mathcal{B}_!$ and remark that $\mathcal{B}_!$ is a laminar family.

nodes.name: Laminar tree induced by a bipartition system
nodes.statement:
Hence, it induces a laminar tree~$T$.
By extension,
we say that~$T$ is \defd{induced by the bipartition system~$(U,\mathcal{B})$} (or simply by~$\mathcal{B}$).

nodes.name: Unrooted laminar trees as {t-edge}-structures
nodes.statement: As the laminar tree $T$ of a bipartition system~$(U,\mathcal{B})$ is undirected, we model $T$ by the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$-structure $\mathbb{T}$ with universe $U_\mathbb{T}=V(T)$ and binary relation $\ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace_\mathbb{T}$ modeling the edge relation of $T$.

nodes.name: From bipartition systems to set systems
nodes.statement:
Let $(U,\mathcal{B})$ be a bipartition system and $a\in U$.
    Then $(U, \mathcal{S}_a)$ is a set system where $\mathcal{S}_a:=\{X: a\notin X \text{ and } \{X,U\setminus X\} \in \mathcal{B}\}\cup \{\{a\},U\}$.
    Moreover, the laminar tree of $(U,\mathcal{B})$ can be obtained from the laminar tree of $(U,\mathcal{S}_a)$ by deleting the root, making node $\{a\}$ adjacent to the node $U\setminus\{a\}$ and making the tree undirected.
nodes.statement_short: Fixing a in U, the sides avoiding a form a set system whose laminar tree, unrooted and rejoined at {a}, is the laminar tree of the bipartition system.
assumptions: Let $(U,\mathcal{B})$ be a bipartition system and $a\in U$.
conclusions: $(U, \mathcal{S}_a)$ is a set system

the laminar tree of $(U,\mathcal{B})$ can be obtained from the laminar tree of $(U,\mathcal{S}_a)$ by deleting the root, making node $\{a\}$ adjacent to the node $U\setminus\{a\}$ and making the tree undirected.
nodes.label: prop:bipartitiveVSpartitive

nodes.name: CMSO[2]-transduction of the laminar tree of a bipartition system
nodes.statement:
Let~$\Sigma$ be an extended vocabulary,
    including a set unary predicate name~$\ensuremath{\mathsf{BIPART}}\xspace$
    and not including the binary relational symbol~$\ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace$.
    There exists a non-deterministic \CMSO[2]-transduction~$\tau$
    such that,
    for each bipartition system~$(U,\mathcal{B})$
    represented as the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{BIPART}}\xspace\}$-structure~$\mathbb{B}$
    and inducing the laminar tree~$T$ with ${L(T)=U}$,
    and for each $\Sigma$-structure~$\mathbb{A}$ with~$\mathbb{B}\sqsubseteq\mathbb{A}$,
    $\tau(\mathbb{A})$ is non-empty
    and every output in~$\tau(\mathbb{A})$ is equal to some $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$-structure $\mathbb{T}$ representing~$T$.
nodes.statement_short: The laminar tree of the strong bipartitions of a bipartition system can be CMSO[2]-transduced from it.
assumptions:
Let~$\Sigma$ be an extended vocabulary,
    including a set unary predicate name~$\ensuremath{\mathsf{BIPART}}\xspace$
    and not including the binary relational symbol~$\ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace$.

for each bipartition system~$(U,\mathcal{B})$
    represented as the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{BIPART}}\xspace\}$-structure~$\mathbb{B}$
    and inducing the laminar tree~$T$ with ${L(T)=U}$
for each $\Sigma$-structure~$\mathbb{A}$ with~$\mathbb{B}\sqsubseteq\mathbb{A}$
conclusions:
$\tau(\mathbb{A})$ is non-empty
    and every output in~$\tau(\mathbb{A})$ is equal to some $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$-structure $\mathbb{T}$ representing~$T$.
nodes.label: lem:transduce laminar tree induced by weakly-bipartitive family

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.2
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathcal{B}$ be a family of bipartitions of $U$ represented as the extended relational structure~$\mathbb{B}$ and $\mathbb{A}$ a $\Sigma$-structure
    with $\mathbb{B}\sqsubseteq \mathbb{A}$. We first use the following two simple atomic \CMSO[2]-transduction to obtain a set system from $(U,\mathcal{B})$.
    Guess any colouring $A$ for which there is a single $a\in U$ with $A(a)$ being satisfied. Interpret using the following formula to obtain a $\ensuremath{\mathsf{SET}}\xspace$-predicate:
    $$\phi_{\ensuremath{\mathsf{SET}}\xspace}(X):=\forall a (A(a)\rightarrow (X=\{a\} \lor X=U \lor a\notin X))\land \ensuremath{\mathsf{BIPART}}\xspace(X,U\setminus X).$$
    The resulting set system $(U,\mathcal{S}_a)$ represented by the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{SET}}\xspace\}$-structure $\mathbb{S}$ is a set system by \autoref{prop:bipartitiveVSpartitive}. Hence, we can use the transduction from \autoref{lem:transduce laminar tree induced by weakly-partitive family} to obtain the $\Sigma\cup\{\mathsf{ancestor}\}$-structure $\mathcal{A}\sqcup \mathcal{T}$ where $\mathcal{T}$ is the $\{\mathsf{ancestor}\}$-structure representing the laminar tree $T$ of $(U,\mathcal{S}_a)$. We now use the following two atomic transductions to obtain the weakly-bipartitive tree of $(U,\mathcal{B})$ according to \autoref{prop:bipartitiveVSpartitive}. We fist restrict the universe to all nodes which are not the root of $\mathbb{T}$. We then interpret using the following formula to obtain the $\ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace$-predicate which makes the graph undirected and adds an edge from $a$ to the node representing the set $U\setminus \{a\}$ which is the root of $T$ after removing the node corresponding to $U$:
    $$\phi_{\ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace}(x,y):=\ensuremath{\mathsf{parent}}\xspace(x,y)\lor \ensuremath{\mathsf{parent}}\xspace(y,x)\lor (x=a \land \lnot \exists z \ensuremath{\mathsf{parent}}\xspace(z,y))\lor (y=a \land \lnot \exists z \ensuremath{\mathsf{parent}}\xspace(z,x)).$$
    Finally, the transduction keeps only $\ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace$ and any $Q\in \Sigma$
    as relations for its output.
nodes.statement_short: Guess an element a, interpret the set system S_a (Lemma 5.1), transduce its laminar tree (Lemma 4.1), then remove the root and reconnect {a}.

nodes.name: Plan: reduce to a set system
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathcal{B}$ be a family of bipartitions of $U$ represented as the extended relational structure~$\mathbb{B}$ and $\mathbb{A}$ a $\Sigma$-structure
    with $\mathbb{B}\sqsubseteq \mathbb{A}$. We first use the following two simple atomic \CMSO[2]-transduction to obtain a set system from $(U,\mathcal{B})$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to a set system with two atomic transductions.

nodes.name: Guess a and interpret S_a
nodes.statement:
Guess any colouring $A$ for which there is a single $a\in U$ with $A(a)$ being satisfied. Interpret using the following formula to obtain a $\ensuremath{\mathsf{SET}}\xspace$-predicate:
    $$\phi_{\ensuremath{\mathsf{SET}}\xspace}(X):=\forall a (A(a)\rightarrow (X=\{a\} \lor X=U \lor a\notin X))\land \ensuremath{\mathsf{BIPART}}\xspace(X,U\setminus X).$$
nodes.statement_short: Guess a single element a and interpret the SET predicate of S_a.

nodes.name: Laminar tree of S_a
nodes.statement: The resulting set system $(U,\mathcal{S}_a)$ represented by the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{SET}}\xspace\}$-structure $\mathbb{S}$ is a set system by \autoref{prop:bipartitiveVSpartitive}. Hence, we can use the transduction from \autoref{lem:transduce laminar tree induced by weakly-partitive family} to obtain the $\Sigma\cup\{\mathsf{ancestor}\}$-structure $\mathcal{A}\sqcup \mathcal{T}$ where $\mathcal{T}$ is the $\{\mathsf{ancestor}\}$-structure representing the laminar tree $T$ of $(U,\mathcal{S}_a)$.
nodes.statement_short: By Lemmas 5.1 and 4.1, transduce the laminar tree of S_a.

nodes.name: Unroot and reconnect
nodes.statement:
We now use the following two atomic transductions to obtain the weakly-bipartitive tree of $(U,\mathcal{B})$ according to \autoref{prop:bipartitiveVSpartitive}. We fist restrict the universe to all nodes which are not the root of $\mathbb{T}$. We then interpret using the following formula to obtain the $\ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace$-predicate which makes the graph undirected and adds an edge from $a$ to the node representing the set $U\setminus \{a\}$ which is the root of $T$ after removing the node corresponding to $U$:
    $$\phi_{\ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace}(x,y):=\ensuremath{\mathsf{parent}}\xspace(x,y)\lor \ensuremath{\mathsf{parent}}\xspace(y,x)\lor (x=a \land \lnot \exists z \ensuremath{\mathsf{parent}}\xspace(z,y))\lor (y=a \land \lnot \exists z \ensuremath{\mathsf{parent}}\xspace(z,x)).$$
nodes.statement_short: Remove the root and define t-edge, joining a to the node U minus a.

nodes.name: Keep t-edge
nodes.statement:
Finally, the transduction keeps only $\ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace$ and any $Q\in \Sigma$
    as relations for its output.
nodes.statement_short: Output only t-edge and the input symbols.

nodes.name: Weakly-bipartitive tree theorem
nodes.statement:
Let~$\mathcal{B}$ be a weakly-bipartitive family,
    $\mathcal{B}_!$ be its subfamily of strong bipartitions,
    and~$T$ the laminar tree it induces.
    There exists a total labeling function~$\lambda$ from the set $V(T)\setminus L(T)$
    of the inner nodes of~$T$ to the set $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{degenerate}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathsf{prime}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathsf{linear}}\xspace\}$, and, for each inner node $t\in \lambda^{-1}(\ensuremath{\mathsf{linear}}\xspace)$, a linear ordering $<_{t}$ of its neighbors, such that every inner node of degree exactly three is labeled by $\ensuremath{\mathsf{degenerate}}\xspace$ and the following conditions are satisfied:
    \begin{itemize}[nosep]
        \item for each bipartition~$\{X,Y\}\in\mathcal{B}\setminus\mathcal{B}_!$,
            there exists~$t\in V(T)\setminus L(T)$
            and a subset~$\mathcal{C}$ of neighbors of~$t$
            such that either $X$ or $Y$ is equal to the set
            $\bigcup_{c\in\mathcal{C}}L(T^t_c)$ and either $\lambda(t)=\ensuremath{\mathsf{linear}}\xspace$ and $\mathcal{C}$ is a $<_t$-interval, or $\lambda(t)=\ensuremath{\mathsf{degenerate}}\xspace$;
        \item conversely,
            for each inner node~$t$
            and each non-empty subset~$\mathcal{C}$, $\mathcal{C}\not= U$ of neighbors of~$t$,
            the bipartition
            $\big\{\bigcup_{c\in\mathcal{C}}L(T^t_c),\bigcup_{c\notin\mathcal{C}}L(T^t_c)\big\}$ is a member of~$\mathcal{B}$ if either $\lambda(t)=\ensuremath{\mathsf{linear}}\xspace$ and $\mathcal{C}$ is $<_t$-interval or $\lambda(t)=\ensuremath{\mathsf{degenerate}}\xspace$.
    \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: The strong-bipartition tree of a weakly-bipartitive family, labeled degenerate/prime/linear with neighbour orders at linear nodes, describes all its bipartitions.
assumptions:
Let~$\mathcal{B}$ be a weakly-bipartitive family,
    $\mathcal{B}_!$ be its subfamily of strong bipartitions,
    and~$T$ the laminar tree it induces.
conclusions: There exists a total labeling function~$\lambda$

nodes.name: Cyclic shift of a linear order
nodes.statement:
We note that the total orders $<_t$ are uniquely determined by
$\mathcal{B}$ up to inverting and cyclic shifting, {\em i.e.}, for a linear order $<$ of $X=\{x_1,\dots,x_\ell\}$ with $x_1<\dots<x_\ell$ we call the order $<'$ of $X$
with $x_\ell<'x_1<'\dots<' x_{\ell-1}$ a \defd{cyclic shift of $<$}.

nodes.name: Weakly-bipartitive tree of a family
nodes.statement:
Neglecting that $<_t$ are only unique up to inverting and cyclic shifting, we represent every weakly-bipartitive family $\mathcal{B}$ by a triple $(T,\lambda,(<_t)_{t\in \lambda^{-1}(\ensuremath{\mathsf{linear}}\xspace)})$ where $T$ is the laminar tree induced by $\mathcal{B}_!$, $\lambda:V(T)\setminus L(T)\to\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{degenerate}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathsf{prime}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathsf{linear}}\xspace\}$ is the labeling function, and $<_t$ is the total order of the neighbours of $t$ described above. Note that in this case $\bigcup_{t\in\lambda^{-1}(\ensuremath{\mathsf{linear}}\xspace)}<_t$ is not a partial order as it is not necessarily transitive.
We call the triple $(T,\lambda,(<_t)_{t\in \lambda^{-1}(\ensuremath{\mathsf{linear}}\xspace)})$ from \autoref{thm:weakly-bipartitive tree} \defd{\strong{the} bipartitive tree} of $\mathcal{B}$.
nodes.statement_short: The triple (T, lambda, (<_t)) from Theorem 5.2, with orders taken up to inversion and cyclic shift.

nodes.name: Weakly-bipartitive trees as {t-edge, degenerate, betweeness}-structures
nodes.statement:
We model weakly-bipartitive trees~$(T,\lambda,(<_t)_{t\in \lambda^{-1}(\ensuremath{\mathsf{linear}}\xspace)})$ of a weakly-bipartitive family $\mathcal{B}$ of bipartition of $U$
by the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathsf{degenerate}}\xspace,\mathsf{betweeness}\}$-structure $\mathbb{T}$
of universe $U_{\mathbb{T}}=V(T)$ such that
$\struct{V(T),\ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace_{\mathbb{T}}}\sqsubseteq\mathbb{T}$ models~$T$ with ${L(T)=U}$,
$\ensuremath{\mathsf{degenerate}}\xspace_{\mathbb{T}}$ is a unary relation
which selects all inner nodes of~$T$ of label~$\ensuremath{\mathsf{degenerate}}\xspace$,
{\em i.e.}, ${\ensuremath{\mathsf{degenerate}}\xspace_{\mathbb{T}}=\lambda^{-1}(\ensuremath{\mathsf{degenerate}}\xspace)}$,
and~$\mathsf{betweeness}_{\mathbb{T}}$ is a relation of arity four selecting all quadruples $(t,x,y,z)$ for which $y$ is between $x$ and $z$ in $<_t$.

nodes.name: MSO-transduction from a weakly-bipartitive tree to its system
nodes.statement:
Furthermore, \autoref{thm:weakly-bipartitive tree},
gives rise to an \ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace-transduction
which takes as input a weakly-bipartitive tree
and outputs the weakly-bipartitive set system which induced it.
conclusions:
gives rise to an \ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace-transduction
which takes as input a weakly-bipartitive tree
and outputs the weakly-bipartitive set system which induced it.

nodes.name: CMSO[2]-transduction of weakly-bipartitive trees
nodes.statement:
There exists a non-deterministic \CMSO[2]-transduction~$\tau$
    such that,
    for every weakly-bipartitive bipartition system~$(U,\mathcal{B})$
    represented as the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{BIPART}}\xspace\}$-structure~$\mathbb{B}$,
    $\tau(\mathbb{B})$ is non-empty and every output in~$\tau(\mathbb{B})$
    is equal to some $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathsf{degenerate}}\xspace,\mathsf{betweeness}\}$-structure~$\mathbb{T}$
    representing the weakly-bipartitive tree~$\left(T,\lambda,(<_t)_{t\in \lambda^{-1}(\ensuremath{\mathsf{linear}}\xspace)}\right)$ of~$(U,\mathcal{B})$.
nodes.statement_short: A non-deterministic CMSO[2]-transduction outputs the weakly-bipartitive tree of any weakly-bipartitive bipartition system.
assumptions:
for every weakly-bipartitive bipartition system~$(U,\mathcal{B})$
    represented as the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{BIPART}}\xspace\}$-structure~$\mathbb{B}$
conclusions:
$\tau(\mathbb{B})$ is non-empty and every output in~$\tau(\mathbb{B})$
    is equal to some
nodes.label: thm:transduce weakly-bipartitive tree

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.3
nodes.statement:
\autoref{lem:transduce laminar tree induced by weakly-bipartitive family} already provides a \CMSO[2]-transduction
    which on input $\mathbb{B}$ outputs the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{BIPART}}\xspace, \ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$-structure $\mathbb{B}\sqcup \mathbb{T}'$,
    where $\mathbb{T}'$ represents the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$-structure modeling the laminar tree $T$ of $(U,\mathcal{B})$.
    To complete the proof of the theorem, we provide an \ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace-transduction which outputs $\mathbb{T}$ given input $\mathbb{B}\sqcup \mathbb{T}'$.
    For the transduction we define an \ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace-formula $\phi_{\ensuremath{\mathsf{degenerate}}\xspace}$ which selects the inner nodes of $T$ which are labeled $\ensuremath{\mathsf{degenerate}}\xspace$,
    and a formula $\phi_{\mathsf{betweeness}}$ which selects quadruples of nodes $(t,x,y,z)$ such that either $x<_t y<_t z$ or $z<_t y<_t x$.
    Recall, that the ordering $<_t$ for each inner node $t$ of the neighbours of $t$ are only unique up to inverting the order and cyclic shift.
    In order to select a representative of $<_t$ which is unique only up to inverting the order, we need non-determinism (details follow).
    We use a functional symbol $\ensuremath{\mathsf{leafset}}\xspace(t,s)$ which is interpreted as the set $L(T_s^t)$.
    The functional predicate $\ensuremath{\mathsf{leafset}}\xspace$ clearly can be defined in \ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace as a element~$z$ belongs to $\ensuremath{\mathsf{leafset}}\xspace(t,s)$
    if and only if\xspace~$z$ is a leaf and the path from~$z$ to~$s$ does not contain~$t$.

    Observe that by \autoref{thm:weakly-bipartitive tree} an inner node $t$ is labeled $\ensuremath{\mathsf{degenerate}}\xspace$
    if and only if\xspace for every pair of neighbours $s_1,s_2$ of $t$ the bipartition $\big\{L(T^t_{s_1})\cup L(T^t_{s_2}),U\setminus \big(L(T^t_{s_1})\cup L(T^t_{s_2})\big)\big\}$ is in $\mathcal{B}$.
    We can define this in \ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace using the following formula:
    \begin{align*}
        \phi_{\ensuremath{\mathsf{degenerate}}\xspace}&(x):=\forall y \forall z\Big(\big(\ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace(x,y)\land \ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace(x,z)\big)\rightarrow\\
        &\ensuremath{\mathsf{BIPART}}\xspace\big(\ensuremath{\mathsf{leafset}}\xspace(x,y)\cup \ensuremath{\mathsf{leafset}}\xspace(x,z), U\setminus (\ensuremath{\mathsf{leafset}}\xspace(x,y)\cup \ensuremath{\mathsf{leafset}}\xspace(x,z))\big)\Big).
    \end{align*}

    By \autoref{thm:weakly-bipartitive tree}, two neighbors~$x$ and~$y$ of~$t$ are consecutive in~$<_t$
    if and only if\xspace, the bipartition $\big\{L(T^t_x)\cup L(T^t_y),U\setminus\big(L(T^t_x)\cup L(T^t_y)\big)\big\}$ is a member of~$\mathcal{B}$
    and at least one of~$x$ or~$y$ is not extremal in~$<_t$.
    Hence, fixing, for each $\ensuremath{\mathsf{linear}}\xspace$-labeled node~$t$,
    the two extremals of~$<_t$ is enough to define~$<_t$ on~$\mathbb{B}\sqcup\mathbb{T'}$ in \ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace.
    To this end, we consider a rooted version of~$T$,
    in which the non-deterministically-guessed root~$r$ is not labeled by~$\ensuremath{\mathsf{linear}}\xspace$,
    and we fix the parent~$p$ of each $\ensuremath{\mathsf{linear}}\xspace$-labeled node~$t$ as the minimum of~$<_t$.
    We also guess a set~$M$ of nodes, such that in~$T$ rooted in~$r$,
    exactly one child~$m$ of each $\ensuremath{\mathsf{linear}}\xspace$-labeled node~$t$ with parent $p$
    belongs to~$M$, and furthermore, the pair $\big\{L(T^t_p)\cup L(T^t_m),U\setminus\big(L(T^t_p)\cup L(T^t_m)\big)\big\}$ is a member of~$\mathcal{B}$.
    Thus, $m$ can be considered as the maximum of~$<_t$.
    Equipped with the relation $\mathsf{ancestor}$ (induced by the rooting of~$T$ in~$r$)
    and the colouring~$M$, we are now able to define $\phi_{\mathsf{betweeness}}$ in \ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace.
    Indeed, for two neighbours $x,y$ of a node $t$ labeled $\ensuremath{\mathsf{linear}}\xspace$, with parent~$p$, and child~$m\in M$, it holds that $x<_t y$ if and only if\xspace
    there is a set~$X$ containing both~$L(T_p^t)$ and~$L(T_x^t)$, excluding~$L(T_y^t)$ and $L(T_m^t)$, and satisfying $(X,U\setminus X)\in\mathcal{B}$.
    Hence, we can define in \ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace, $x<_t y$ as follows:
    \begin{align*}
        &x<_t y:=\exists p \exists m \Big[\ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace(t,x)\land\ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace(t,y)\land
            \ensuremath{\mathsf{parent}}\xspace(p,t)\land \ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace(t,m) \land M(m) \land
             \exists X\exists Y
             \\*
            &\Big(\ensuremath{\mathsf{BIPART}}\xspace(X,Y)\land\big(\ensuremath{\mathsf{leafset}}\xspace(t,p)\cup \ensuremath{\mathsf{leafset}}\xspace(t,x)\big)\subseteq X\land \big(\ensuremath{\mathsf{leafset}}\xspace(t,y)\cup \ensuremath{\mathsf{leafset}}\xspace(t,m)\big)\subseteq Y\Big)\Big].
    \end{align*}
    Note that any node with a child in $M$ must necessarily be labeled $\ensuremath{\mathsf{linear}}\xspace$ and hence:
    \begin{align*}
        \phi_{\mathsf{betweeness}}(t,x,y,z)&:= (x<_t y<_t z)\lor(z<_t y<_t x).
    \end{align*}
    Finally, the transduction forgets the predicate $\ensuremath{\mathsf{BIPART}}\xspace$ to produce the output $\mathbb{T}$.
nodes.statement_short: Transduce the laminar tree (Lemma 5.2), MSO-define degenerate nodes, and fix the cyclic orders at linear nodes by guessing a root and a set M of maximal neighbours. Consecutiveness in <_t is characterised by membership in B of unions of two neighbour leaf sets.

nodes.name: Laminar tree via Lemma 5.2
nodes.statement:
\autoref{lem:transduce laminar tree induced by weakly-bipartitive family} already provides a \CMSO[2]-transduction
    which on input $\mathbb{B}$ outputs the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{BIPART}}\xspace, \ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$-structure $\mathbb{B}\sqcup \mathbb{T}'$,
    where $\mathbb{T}'$ represents the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$-structure modeling the laminar tree $T$ of $(U,\mathcal{B})$.
    To complete the proof of the theorem, we provide an \ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace-transduction which outputs $\mathbb{T}$ given input $\mathbb{B}\sqcup \mathbb{T}'$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 5.2 gives the laminar tree; an MSO-transduction remains.

nodes.name: Formulas and leafset
nodes.statement:
For the transduction we define an \ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace-formula $\phi_{\ensuremath{\mathsf{degenerate}}\xspace}$ which selects the inner nodes of $T$ which are labeled $\ensuremath{\mathsf{degenerate}}\xspace$,
    and a formula $\phi_{\mathsf{betweeness}}$ which selects quadruples of nodes $(t,x,y,z)$ such that either $x<_t y<_t z$ or $z<_t y<_t x$.
    Recall, that the ordering $<_t$ for each inner node $t$ of the neighbours of $t$ are only unique up to inverting the order and cyclic shift.
    In order to select a representative of $<_t$ which is unique only up to inverting the order, we need non-determinism (details follow).
    We use a functional symbol $\ensuremath{\mathsf{leafset}}\xspace(t,s)$ which is interpreted as the set $L(T_s^t)$.
    The functional predicate $\ensuremath{\mathsf{leafset}}\xspace$ clearly can be defined in \ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace as a element~$z$ belongs to $\ensuremath{\mathsf{leafset}}\xspace(t,s)$
    if and only if\xspace~$z$ is a leaf and the path from~$z$ to~$s$ does not contain~$t$.
nodes.statement_short: Plan degenerate and betweeness formulas; leafset(t,s) is MSO-definable; orders need non-determinism.

nodes.name: Define degenerate
nodes.statement:
Observe that by \autoref{thm:weakly-bipartitive tree} an inner node $t$ is labeled $\ensuremath{\mathsf{degenerate}}\xspace$
    if and only if\xspace for every pair of neighbours $s_1,s_2$ of $t$ the bipartition $\big\{L(T^t_{s_1})\cup L(T^t_{s_2}),U\setminus \big(L(T^t_{s_1})\cup L(T^t_{s_2})\big)\big\}$ is in $\mathcal{B}$.
    We can define this in \ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace using the following formula:
    \begin{align*}
        \phi_{\ensuremath{\mathsf{degenerate}}\xspace}&(x):=\forall y \forall z\Big(\big(\ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace(x,y)\land \ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace(x,z)\big)\rightarrow\\
        &\ensuremath{\mathsf{BIPART}}\xspace\big(\ensuremath{\mathsf{leafset}}\xspace(x,y)\cup \ensuremath{\mathsf{leafset}}\xspace(x,z), U\setminus (\ensuremath{\mathsf{leafset}}\xspace(x,y)\cup \ensuremath{\mathsf{leafset}}\xspace(x,z))\big)\Big).
    \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: t is degenerate iff every union of two neighbour leaf sets yields a bipartition in B.

nodes.name: Consecutiveness criterion
nodes.statement:
By \autoref{thm:weakly-bipartitive tree}, two neighbors~$x$ and~$y$ of~$t$ are consecutive in~$<_t$
    if and only if\xspace, the bipartition $\big\{L(T^t_x)\cup L(T^t_y),U\setminus\big(L(T^t_x)\cup L(T^t_y)\big)\big\}$ is a member of~$\mathcal{B}$
    and at least one of~$x$ or~$y$ is not extremal in~$<_t$.
    Hence, fixing, for each $\ensuremath{\mathsf{linear}}\xspace$-labeled node~$t$,
    the two extremals of~$<_t$ is enough to define~$<_t$ on~$\mathbb{B}\sqcup\mathbb{T'}$ in \ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace.
nodes.statement_short: Consecutive neighbours are detected via B; fixing the two extremes determines <_t.

nodes.name: Guess root and M
nodes.statement:
To this end, we consider a rooted version of~$T$,
    in which the non-deterministically-guessed root~$r$ is not labeled by~$\ensuremath{\mathsf{linear}}\xspace$,
    and we fix the parent~$p$ of each $\ensuremath{\mathsf{linear}}\xspace$-labeled node~$t$ as the minimum of~$<_t$.
    We also guess a set~$M$ of nodes, such that in~$T$ rooted in~$r$,
    exactly one child~$m$ of each $\ensuremath{\mathsf{linear}}\xspace$-labeled node~$t$ with parent $p$
    belongs to~$M$, and furthermore, the pair $\big\{L(T^t_p)\cup L(T^t_m),U\setminus\big(L(T^t_p)\cup L(T^t_m)\big)\big\}$ is a member of~$\mathcal{B}$.
    Thus, $m$ can be considered as the maximum of~$<_t$.
nodes.statement_short: Guess a non-linear root (parent is minimum) and a set M giving the maximum.

nodes.name: Define <_t
nodes.statement:
Equipped with the relation $\mathsf{ancestor}$ (induced by the rooting of~$T$ in~$r$)
    and the colouring~$M$, we are now able to define $\phi_{\mathsf{betweeness}}$ in \ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace.
    Indeed, for two neighbours $x,y$ of a node $t$ labeled $\ensuremath{\mathsf{linear}}\xspace$, with parent~$p$, and child~$m\in M$, it holds that $x<_t y$ if and only if\xspace
    there is a set~$X$ containing both~$L(T_p^t)$ and~$L(T_x^t)$, excluding~$L(T_y^t)$ and $L(T_m^t)$, and satisfying $(X,U\setminus X)\in\mathcal{B}$.
    Hence, we can define in \ensuremath{\operatorname{MSO}}\xspace, $x<_t y$ as follows:
    \begin{align*}
        &x<_t y:=\exists p \exists m \Big[\ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace(t,x)\land\ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace(t,y)\land
            \ensuremath{\mathsf{parent}}\xspace(p,t)\land \ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace(t,m) \land M(m) \land
             \exists X\exists Y
             \\*
            &\Big(\ensuremath{\mathsf{BIPART}}\xspace(X,Y)\land\big(\ensuremath{\mathsf{leafset}}\xspace(t,p)\cup \ensuremath{\mathsf{leafset}}\xspace(t,x)\big)\subseteq X\land \big(\ensuremath{\mathsf{leafset}}\xspace(t,y)\cup \ensuremath{\mathsf{leafset}}\xspace(t,m)\big)\subseteq Y\Big)\Big].
    \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Define x <_t y via a bipartition separating p, x from y, m.

nodes.name: Define betweeness and output
nodes.statement_short: Betweeness from <_t; forget BIPART.

nodes.name: Bipartitive families have no linear nodes
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{B}$ be a weakly-biaprtitive family and let \linebreak $(T,\lambda,(<_t)_{t\in \lambda^{-1}(\ensuremath{\mathsf{linear}}\xspace)})$ be the weakly-bipartitive tree it induces. If $\mathcal{B}$ is bipartitive, then $\lambda^{-1}(\ensuremath{\mathsf{linear}}\xspace)=\emptyset$ and all $<_t$ are empty.
assumptions: Let $\mathcal{B}$ be a weakly-biaprtitive family
$\mathcal{B}$ is bipartitive
conclusions: $\lambda^{-1}(\ensuremath{\mathsf{linear}}\xspace)=\emptyset$ and all $<_t$ are empty.

nodes.name: Bipartitive tree
nodes.statement: As a consequence, we can capture any bipartitive family $\mathcal{B}$ by the simpler structure $(T,\lambda)$, called the \emph{bipartitive tree induced by $\mathcal{B}$} (or \emph{or the bipartitive tree of $\mathcal{B}$}), where $\lambda$ is now a labeling function labeling each inner nodes of $T$ by either $\ensuremath{\mathsf{degenerate}}\xspace$ or $\ensuremath{\mathsf{prime}}\xspace$.

nodes.name: Derivation of Corollary 5.4
nodes.statement: Hence, we obtain the following as a corollary from \autoref{thm:transduce weakly-bipartitive tree}, where naturally the bipartitive tree $(T,\lambda)$ of a bipartitive family $\mathcal{B}$ is modeled by a $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathsf{degenerate}}\xspace\}$-structure $\mathbb{B}$.
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from Theorem 5.3 since bipartitive trees have no linear nodes.

There exists a non-deterministic \CMSO[2]-transduction $\tau$ such that,
    for each bipartitive set system $(U,\mathcal{B})$ represented as the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{BIPART}}\xspace\}$-structure $\mathbb{B}$,
    $\tau(\mathbb{B})$ is non-empty and every output in~$\tau(\mathbb{B})$
    is equal to some $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathsf{degenerate}}\xspace\}$-structure $\mathbb{T}$ representing the bipartitive tree $(T,\ensuremath{\mathsf{degenerate}}\xspace)$ of~$(U,\mathcal{B})$.

nodes.name: Split of a directed graph
nodes.statement:
Let $G$ be a directed graph.
A \emph{split} in $G$ is a bipartition $\{X,Y\}$ of $V(G)$ such that there are subsets $X^{\operatorname{in}},X^{\operatorname{out}}\subseteq X$, $Y^{\operatorname{in}},Y^{\operatorname{out}}\subseteq Y$ such that for all pairs of vertices $x\in X$ and $y\in Y$ the edge $xy\in E(G)$ if and only if\xspace either $x\in X^{\operatorname{out}}$ and $y\in Y^{\operatorname{in}}$ or $x\in Y^{\operatorname{out}}$ and $y\in X^{\operatorname{in}}$.
nodes.statement_short: A bipartition {X,Y} where edges across are exactly those from an out-part of one side to an in-part of the other.

nodes.name: Trivial split
nodes.statement: We call splits $\{X,Y\}$ for which either $|X|=1$ or $|Y|=1$ \emph{trivial splits}.

nodes.name: Strong split
nodes.statement: In a family $\mathcal{B}$ of splits we use the notion of \emph{strong splits} to coincide with the notion of strong bipartitions.

nodes.name: Marker vertices
nodes.statement: With a split $\{X,Y\}$ in a connected graph $G$ we associate the following decomposition of $G$ into graphs $G_X$ and $G_Y$. Let $v_X^Y,v_Y^X\notin V(G)$ be two new vertices, called \emph{marker vertices}.

nodes.name: Split components G_X and G_Y
nodes.statement: Define $G_X$ to be the graph obtained by adding $v_X^Y$ to $G[X]$ and edge $xv_X^Y$ for every $x\in X^{\operatorname{out}}$ and edge $v_X^Yx$ for every $x\in X^{\operatorname{in}}$. The graph $G_Y$ is defined equivalently.

nodes.name: Split decomposition
nodes.statement: We can recursively decompose $G$ along splits to obtain a decomposition into graphs $G_1,\dots, G_k$. We call such a decomposition of $G$ into graphs $G_1,\dots, G_k$ a \emph{split decomposition} if every graph $G_i$ is either a singleton consisting of an original (not a marker) vertex or does not have any non-trivial split.

nodes.name: Components of a split decomposition
nodes.statement: We call the graphs $G_i$ \emph{components} of the split decomposition.

nodes.name: Enriched split decomposition
nodes.statement: To be able to reconstruct the graph, we represent a split decomposition of $G$ into graphs $G_1,\dots, G_k$ by an \emph{enriched split decomposition} which is a pair $(H,F)$ consisting of a directed graph $H$ with an additional (symmetric) edge relation $F$. The graph $H$ consisting of the disjoint union $G_1,\dots,G_k$. The edge relation $F$ contains an (undirected) edge between every pair of markers corresponding to one step of the decomposition.
nodes.statement_short: A pair (H, F): the disjoint union H of the components plus an edge relation F joining paired marker vertices.

nodes.name: c-edges and t-edges
nodes.statement: For a clear distinction, we call the edges in $H$ \emph{$\mathsf{c}$-edges} and the edges in $F$ \emph{$\mathsf{t}$-edges}.

nodes.name: Splits form a weakly-bipartitive family
nodes.statement: If $G$ is connected then the family of splits of $G$ is weakly-bipartitive.
assumptions: $G$ is connected
conclusions: the family of splits of $G$ is weakly-bipartitive.

nodes.name: Canonical split decomposition
nodes.statement: Hence, there is a unique split decomposition of $G$, which is called the \emph{canonical split decomposition} of $G$, in which we only decompose along strong splits.

nodes.name: Edges in an enriched split decomposition
nodes.statement_short: Edges of G are alternating c/t-paths in the enriched split decomposition; marker c-edges reflect edges of G between the corresponding sides.
assumptions: Let $G$ be a connected, directed graph and $(H,F)$ an enriched split decomposition of $G$.
conclusions: $uv\in E(G)$ if and only if\xspace there exists a directed path from $u$ to $v$ in $(H,F)$ on which $\textsf{c}$-edges and $\textsf{t}$-edges alternate;
nodes.label: lem:edgesInSplitDecomposition

nodes.name: Enriched split decompositions as {t-edge, c-edge}-structures
nodes.statement: To model enriched split decompositions as relational structures we use the relational vocabulary $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathsf{c}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$ where $\ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace$ and $\ensuremath{\mathsf{c}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace$ are binary relational symbols. Am enriched split decomposition $(H,F)$ of a graph $G$ is the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathsf{c}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$-relation $\mathbb{H}$ with universe $U_\mathbb{H}=V(H)$, $\ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace_\mathbb{H}$ the set of $\textsf{t}$-edges in $(H,F)$ and $\ensuremath{\mathsf{c}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace_{\mathbb{H}}$ the set of $\textsf{c}$-edges of $(H,F)$.

nodes.name: CMSO[2]-transduction of the canonical split decomposition
nodes.statement:
There exists a non-deterministic \CMSO[2]-transduction $\tau$
    such that for any connected, directed graph $G$ represented as the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$-structure $\mathbb{G}$;
    $\tau(\mathbb{G})$ is non-empty
    and every output in~$\tau(\mathbb{G})$ is equal to some $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{t}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathsf{c}\text-\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$-structure $\mathbb{H}$
    representing the canonical split decomposition of $G$.
nodes.statement_short: A non-deterministic CMSO[2]-transduction outputs the canonical (enriched) split decomposition of any connected directed graph.
assumptions: for any connected, directed graph $G$ represented as the $\{\ensuremath{\mathsf{edge}}\xspace\}$-structure $\mathbb{G}$
conclusions:
$\tau(\mathbb{G})$ is non-empty
    and every output in~$\tau(\mathbb{G})$ is equal to some
nodes.label: thm:split

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.6
nodes.statement_short: Define splits in MSO, transduce their laminar tree (Lemma 5.2), represent each marker by a tree node or its copy after guessing a root, and define c-edges via Lemma 5.5.

nodes.name: Associated structures

nodes.name: Split system

nodes.statement_short: The laminar tree of the splits.
